To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a carefully monitored high dose urogram is a valuable tool in the management of patients who are in shock following severe injury.
in severely injured patients with renal injuries, preoperative urograms can be obtained with a carefully monitored high dosage urographic procedure.
in hypotensive trauma patients, the preoperative excretory urogram can be obtained with high quality if the patients are properly resuscitated.

the development of a new approach to the study of the preoperative urograph.
the study of the effects of shock on renal hemodynamics and function.
the development of a protocol for the preoperative evaluation of patients with severe trauma who are at risk of renal injury.

in the severely injured patient, hypotensive or not, a urologic evaluation is mandatory.
the use of high-dosage contrast urography is a safe, effective, and reliable diagnostic procedure for the detection of renal injuries in patients with shock.
a high-dosage excretory urogram is a safe procedure in the severely injured patient and can be performed with a high rate of success.
